supported_scope: A conditional obstruction for systems with an actually uniform positive pure-slice slope and all other stated structural comparison hypotheses.
exact_claim: For a multiplicative Taylor-leaf graded system with N_j~c_X*j^n, n>=1 and c_X>0, a fixed uniform pure-slice lower bound b_0(h)>=sigma*h-C, sigma>0, a uniformly bounded cube, fixed nonnegative transverse weights, the tangent-variation upper bound, scaled-test comparison, uniform discrepancy bound a>=0 and a positive liminf sequence, persistent positive-dimensional minimizers imply sigma*(t+a/(n+2))<=n+1.
hypotheses: A fixed slope sigma>0 and growth constants/thresholds uniform across moving reference tests
A cube realized in uniformly bounded degree
Nonnegative weights independent of auxiliary degree
T_m<=d/t from the stated tangent-variation premise
Scaled-test comparison with linear discrepancy scaling and lower bound a
A fixed positive t and a positive-liminf sequence
decisive_argument: Replace the slice increment by sigma*h-(C+sigma*h_0); normalized partition increments tend to sigma/l, yielding the exact sigma-bearing premise of the formal scalar obstruction.
argument_assessment: The homogeneous sigma factor, derivation of the lower moment and all-length limit extraction are correct under uniform structural hypotheses. The abstract hypotheses are not themselves formalized or established by examples.
external_assumptions: Compact-set Brunn-Minkowski and simplex comparison for a Taylor-lattice realization
execution_scope: The scalar theorem was freshly compiled; no new system, enlarged experiment or geometric realization was attempted.
